---
title: "7 · Model validation and performance assessment"
description: "Cross-validation done properly for spatial and temporal data, and choosing measures that match the scientific objective."
categories: [validation, metrics, spatial-temporal, uncertainty]
---

A performance number is a claim about the future: *this is roughly how well the model
will do on data it has not seen.* Validation is the process of earning the right to
make that claim.

Done casually, it produces flattering nonsense. Randomly splitting autocorrelated
survey data puts near-identical observations on both sides of the split, so the model
is tested on what it has effectively already seen. Reporting accuracy on a problem
where the positive class is two per cent of the data rewards a model that never
predicts it at all.

This section covers doing it properly, and choosing measures that reflect what you
actually care about — which is rarely the default.

## In this section

- Cross-validation
- Spatial and temporal cross-validation
- Regression performance measures
- Classification performance measures
- Confusion matrix, precision, recall, and related measures
